from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[0, 120, 20], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 20 * x, x_range=[0, 5], color="#00FF00")
        group = VGroup(axes, graph)
        self.place_in_area(group, 'B3', 'E6', scale_factor=0.4)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "We shrink the time interval toward zero.",
            "Secant line connects two points.",
            "As points approach, the interval closes.",
            "The secant line becomes a tangent line.",
            "This reveals the rate at one instant."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Limit Approach: From Secant to Tangent", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup Axes and Curve
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], tips=False).scale(0.5)
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.25 * x**2, color="#FFFF00")
        curve_group = VGroup(axes, curve)
        self.place_in_area(curve_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)

        # Mobjects
        point_a = Dot(axes.c2p(1, 0.25), color="#00FFFF")
        point_b = Dot(axes.c2p(3, 2.25), color="#00FFFF")
        
        # Secant line updater
        secant = always_redraw(lambda: Line(point_a.get_center(), point_b.get_center(), color="#FF00FF"))

        # ValueTracker for B movement
        t_b = ValueTracker(3)
        point_b.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(axes.c2p(t_b.get_value(), 0.25 * t_b.get_value()**2)))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(Create(curve_group))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.add(point_a, point_b, secant)
        self.play(FadeIn(point_a), FadeIn(point_b), Create(secant))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(t_b.animate.set_value(1.1), run_time=3)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(t_b.animate.set_value(1.01), run_time=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Derivative is the limit of the secant.", 
            "Definition uses h approaching zero.", 
            "It calculates slope at a single point.", 
            "For x squared, the slope is 4.", 
            "This is the instantaneous speed."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Derivative", lecture_lines)
        
        formula = MathTex(
            "f'(x) = \\lim_{h \\to 0} \\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}",
            font_size=40
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B2', 'C5', scale_factor=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display formula
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight f(x+h) - f(x)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF8C00")
        sub_formula = formula[0][8:16] 
        self.play(Indicate(sub_formula, color="#FF8C00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight h
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#7FFF00")
        denom_h = formula[0][18]
        self.play(Indicate(denom_h, color="#7FFF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Animate h shrinking
        self.lecture[3].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(formula.animate.set_color(BLUE), run_time=1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Blink notation
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(Flash(formula[0][0:4], color=WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", [
            "Derivative equals the tangent line's slope.",
            "Average change versus instantaneous focus.",
            "Derivative provides precision for engineering."
        ])
        
        # Visuals
        summary_graph = VGroup(
            Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.5),
            FunctionGraph(lambda x: x**2 / 4, x_range=[0, 4]).set_color(BLUE)
        )
        
        derivative_formula = MathTex(r"f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}").scale(0.8)
        takeaway = Text("Derivative = Precision", font_size=32)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(summary_graph, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(summary_graph))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(derivative_formula, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(derivative_formula))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        derivative_formula.set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(summary_graph), FadeOut(derivative_formula))
        self.place_at_grid(takeaway, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(takeaway))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Average Speed Paradox
sections.content: Define average rate of change as the slope of the secant line over an interval. Use a visual of a cheetah chasing prey to show that 'average speed' hides the dramatic sprints and pauses during the hunt.
sections.example: A cheetah runs 100 meters in 5 seconds. Average speed is 20m/s, but at exactly 2 seconds, was it accelerating or slowing down?

sections.title: The Limit Approach: From Secant to Tangent
sections.content: Introduce the visual 'shrinking interval' animation. As the two points on the curve get infinitely close (Δt → 0), the secant line morphs into a tangent line at a single point.
sections.example: An animation showing two points on a parabolic curve moving toward each other until they overlap, visually transforming the chord into a tangent line.

sections.title: Defining the Derivative
sections.content: Introduce the formal definition: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Explain this as the 'instantaneous speed' or the slope of the tangent line at exactly point x.
sections.example: Graph of y = x²; show the slope calculation at x=2 transitioning from a secant slope of 5 to the tangent slope of 4.

sections.title: Application: The Robot's Velocity
sections.content: Demonstrate the utility of the derivative. If a cleaning robot's position is a function of time, the derivative allows us to know its exact velocity at any micro-second, preventing it from bumping into walls.
sections.example: A smart robot's position function p(t) = 3t²; calculating p'(t) = 6t to find the robot's exact velocity at t=3 seconds.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: Derivative = Slope of tangent line = Instantaneous rate of change. Emphasize that while average change looks at the 'big picture,' the derivative provides the 'precise focus' needed for physics and engineering.
sections.example: A 10-second summary animation showing a car speedometer needle moving in sync with the calculated derivative of its position function.
